sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for Winter Danger Spots, Dawn and Night Driving, Freeway Driving and Emergency Procedures

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A05
In a blowout the brakes stay off until the car is very slow, while in a complete brake failure the first move is to pump the pedal quickly [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint tire-and-brake-emergencies; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F19 and sec15-F22.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A07
In a skid you steer in the direction the rear is sliding and release the brakes, while off the pavement edge you keep straight, slow gently and steer back only at a safe speed [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint control-recovery; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F33 and sec15-F25.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A04
A missed freeway exit means continuing to the next exit [A04], while needing the opposite direction means leaving at the next exit and re-entering, never crossing the divider or turning around [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint freeway; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec15-F15 and sec15-F13.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A02
A congested entrance lane calls for slowing or stopping near its beginning, while a clear entrance lane calls for signaling and accelerating to match freeway speed before merging [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint freeway; prereq_hint sec15-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F09 and sec15-F10.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A01
Before sunrise and after sunset you should turn on low-beam headlamps so others can see you, while if an oncoming vehicle's lights are too bright at night you should flash your high beams once and look toward the right edge of the road [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint night-driving; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F03 and sec15-F06.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A06
An oncoming vehicle in your lane is met by flashing, honking and steering right, while an overtaking vehicle in trouble is helped by steering right and adjusting your speed to its driver's intention [A06].
Why it matters: group_hint head-on-avoidance; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F27 and sec15-F26.
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A07
A stuck accelerator is answered by slapping the pedal and switching the engine off short of the steering lock, while power steering failure is answered simply by extra effort, reduced speed and a safe stop [A07].
Why it matters: group_hint power-emergencies; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F29 and sec15-F30.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A08
A small vehicle fire is smothered with an extinguisher, dirt, sand or a blanket, while a large gasoline or oil fire is left to the professionals and water is never used on fuel or electrical fires [A08].
Why it matters: group_hint fire; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec15-F36 and sec15-F35.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A08
After a breakdown occupants stay in the vehicle unless a reachable safe spot exists, while on a freeway no one walks at all and everyone waits with the vehicle [A08].
Why it matters: group_hint breakdowns; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F37 and sec15-F39.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A03
Through freeway traffic uses the left and center lanes near the posted limit, while the right lane is for slower vehicles and for entering and leaving traffic [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint freeway; prereq_hint sec15-R04; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec15-F11 and sec15-F12.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A04
Emergency braking is maximum pressure released whenever a wheel slides, while antilock brakes perform that release automatically [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint tire-and-brake-emergencies; prereq_hint sec15-R01; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec15-F17 and sec15-F16.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0080]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A05
A lost wheel is handled like a blowout but usually brings brake failure and a tow, while a blowout alone can be driven slowly to safety without rim damage [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint tire-and-brake-emergencies; prereq_hint sec15-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec15-F20 and sec15-F19.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0081]
